content: 1. Discard this product when it has expired or is no longer needed. 2. The information provided here was last updated in September 2024. 3. This document is a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. 4. This information does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. 5. This document is not a substitute for personalized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. 6. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: 7. This medication is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. 8. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. 9. Tipranavir belongs to a class of drugs called protease inhibitors. 10. It must be taken with ritonavir, another protease inhibitor, to enhance (boost) the levels of tipranavir in your body. 11. Tipranavir is not a cure for HIV infection. 12. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 13. Use effective barrier methods (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms/dental dams) during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. 14. Do not share personal items (e.g., needles, syringes, toothbrushes, razors) that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. How to Use: 15. Read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting tipranavir and each time you get a refill. 16. Take this medication by mouth as directed by your doctor, usually twice daily. 17. Swallow the capsules whole. 18. Tipranavir must be taken at the same time as ritonavir. 19. It is crucial to take this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 20. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. 21. Do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed, and do not stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without your doctor’s approval, even for a short time. Side Effects: 22. Common side effects may include diarrhea, nausea, drowsiness, dizziness, headache, or vomiting. 23. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. 24. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. 25. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. 26. These reactions can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. 27. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication (e.g., increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas, decreased fat in the arms and legs). 28. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. 29. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. 30. Tipranavir can commonly cause a mild rash, which is usually not serious. 31. However, it may be difficult to distinguish a mild rash from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. 32. Seek medical attention immediately if you develop a rash. 33. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. Precautions: 34. Before taking tipranavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to sulfa drugs, or if you have any other allergies. 35. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. 36. This drug may cause dizziness or drowsiness. 37. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. 38. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. 39. Limit alcoholic beverages. 40. This drug may rarely cause an increase in blood sugar levels, which can lead to or worsen diabetes. 41. If you already have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. 42. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. 43. This medication may make you more sensitive to sunlight. 44. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. 45. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. 46. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and tipranavir may be part of that treatment. 47. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: 48. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. 49. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. 50. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 51. Other medications can affect the removal of tipranavir from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. 52. Examples include apalutamide, macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), rifampin, and St. John’s Wort. 53. Tipranavir with ritonavir can both speed up and slow down the removal of other drugs from your body, affecting their effectiveness. 54. Aspirin can increase the risk of bleeding when used with this medication. 55. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take low-dose aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (usually 81-162 milligrams daily), continue taking it unless advised otherwise. 56. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods (e.g., pills, patch, ring), potentially leading to pregnancy. 57. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. Overdose: 58. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. 59. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. 60. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Storage: 61. Store unopened bottles in the refrigerator. 62. After opening the bottle, capsules may be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture. 63. Do not store this medication in the bathroom. 64. Once the bottle is opened, this medication expires after 60 days. 65. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. 66. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: 67. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized information about this product and your health needs.
